title: Reservation-to-Elasticity Roadmap and Success Criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers with reserved GPU capacity need predictable throughput but also want elastic behavior to handle transient traffic spikes without manual reservation changes. Our objective this quarter is to define a pragmatic roadmap that moves from static reservations toward a validated, low-risk elasticity model (prefix: 'reservation->elasticity') that protects committed economics while providing fast, observable surge capacity. This ticket captures the roadmap, measurable success criteria, experiment plan, rollout guardrails, and runbook for the initial Q2 pilot.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Product spec for reservation-to-elasticity model approved by Eng, Infra and Sales. (2) Pilot config and canary criteria defined and documented. (3) Two pilot customers onboarded to feature flag with end-to-end metrics in dashboard. (4) Latency and cost regressions bounded (<=5% median latency increase at 95th percentile; cost per token change tracked and acceptable to customers). (5) Rollback strategy and incident playbook published.
milestones: Milestone 1 — Spec & trade-offs: Complete product spec, guardrails, SLA mapping (target 2025-02-28)
Milestone 2 — Implementation & infra: Kernel scheduling hooks + surge pool orchestrator proof-of-concept (target 2025-03-21)
Milestone 3 — Pilot launch: Two customers live on feature flag; monitoring dashboards and churn/quality checks enabled (target 2025-04-11)
Milestone 4 — Readout & decision: Post-pilot metrics review, go/no-go for wide rollout and pricing adjustments (target 2025-04-25)
notes: Design constraints: Must preserve reserved capacity economics for committed customers; elasticity cannot cannibalize reserved revenue under normal conditions.
Policy decision: Elastic capacity will be billed as 'surge credits' with time-bucketed accounting to preserve transparency to customers and internal finance reconciliation.
SLOs: Maintain 99.9% availability for reserved pool requests; P95 latency target unchanged for reserved SLA tier.
Observability needs: token-level costing, model-variant routing counts, surge-pool utilization heatmap, and KSAT traces for long-tail latency.
Edge case: Preemption and eviction policy when demand exceeds combined reserved+surge capacity — define fair-share semantics across customers and tiers.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Elastic surge could undercut reserved revenue or cause customer confusion. Mitigation: clear naming, billing as 'surge credits', and opt-in pilot followed by controlled opt-out windows.

Risk: Increased tail latency when mixing reserved and surge workloads. Mitigation: allocate dedicated lanes or priority-aware scheduling; implement kernel and KV cache isolation experiments in ENG-33210.
Risk: Operational overload for oncall. Mitigation: synthetic load tests, runbook automation, and pre-scheduled rehearsals during pilot window.
Risk: Billing reconciliation complexity. Mitigation: build simple time-bucket counter instrumented into the serving runtime and validate against customer invoices during pilot.
